h1: Integrate Playground Equipment with Natural Landscaping

props.title: Integrate Playground Equipment with Natural Landscaping
props.summaryText: For landscape architects and builders: how to use slopes, mounds, trees and planting in a play area, and the technical details (levels, drainage, root zones) that make it work.
props.author: rohan-mehta
props.imageAlt: Wood-finish play structure set among plants and a pergola in a landscaped garden

takeaways.text: Use the landform: slopes and mounds can carry slides, climbing walls and lookouts.
Agree finished levels, surfacing build-up and drainage with the landscape contractor early.
Keep planting and tree root zones outside safety zones and foundations.
Edges matter: where turf, rubber and planting meet, detail them so they do not trip or wash out.

faq.q: How do you integrate a playground into a sloping site?
faq.a: Use the slope rather than flattening it: slides can run down a bank, climbing walls can face it, and lookouts can sit at the top. Retain and drain the slope properly and keep safety zones clear at the bottom.

faq.q: How close can planting be to playground equipment?
faq.a: Planting should stay outside each item's safety zone. Choose non-toxic, thornless plants and keep branches from overhanging platforms or swing paths.

faq.q: Who coordinates playground and landscape work on site?
faq.a: Usually the landscape architect, with the playground supplier and landscape contractor agreeing levels, surfacing, drainage and sequence before work begins.
